items.summary: We analyze the transport of portfolio exposures between moving subspaces under a varying positive definite risk metric. The reference evolution is the induced connection obtained from the ambient connection of minimum norm in fixed asset coordinates. An explicit expansion of risk weighted Procrustes identifies a leading local error that couples metric deformation with covariant motion normal to the subspace. A rank two construction with an exact continuous solution shows that this term can reduce global accuracy to first order even when the metric commutes with its derivative. Geometric mean alignment and a symmetric Procrustes construction cancel the term and yield reversible updates with second order global accuracy. We establish uniform error bounds on nonuniform partitions, characterize the cases in which the Procrustes defect…

items.summary: We propose a conservative, semi-implicit nonstandard finite difference scheme for the reaction--diffusion equation $u_t=λ(|u_x|^{p-2}u_x)_x+f(u)$, $p>1$, where, as is customary, the $p$-Laplacian is regularized by a parameter $\eps>0$. The scheme combines a denominator function, a lagged diffusion coefficient, and a nonlocal treatment of the loss part of the reaction. For every time step and mesh size we prove that the scheme is well posed and positive, that it preserves an invariant region $[0,K]$ whenever the reaction admits one, and that it reproduces every constant equilibrium exactly. Without reaction, it conserves mass, satisfies a discrete maximum principle, and, for $1 2$. The truncation error is $O(k+h^2)$ at interior nodes. Numerical tests confirm first order in time and second order in space, and show that the scheme remains…
items.title: Unconditionally Positive Nonstandard Finite Difference Schemes for $p$-Laplacian Reaction--Diffusion Equations

items.summary: Large language model (LLM) judges are increasingly used to monitor the outputs of LLM-based AI agents, yet formal guarantees on the reliability of these judges remain largely absent, limiting confidence in their use for safety-critical oversight. We consider certifying such a judge and define its risk over safety classifications of prompt--response pairs drawn from a deployed generator. We apply a PAC-Bayes framework to this setting, refining existing compression-based methodology with the use of tighter bounds and more efficient coding. We show that standard parameter-efficient fine-tuning can yield non-vacuous and even tight certificates for safety judges, for both classification and Brier risk, without holding out data for validation. We introduce LoRA-GT, which shares a single quantisation scale across layers and achieves the…
items.title: Tight PAC-Bayes Generalisation Guarantees for Large Language Model Judges

items.summary: We develop an adaptive numerical method for linear Fokker--Planck equations on $\mathbb R^d$, based on approximating the evolving probability density by linear combinations of Gaussian functions (LCGs). The method applies to polynomial-type drift fields, without requiring a gradient-flow structure or a stationary distribution. It relies on an operator splitting that separates diffusion and affine drift, for which Gaussian functions can be propagated exactly, from higher-order transport, whose evolution is approximated adaptively by LCGs. Both the number of Gaussian components and their means and covariances are adjusted to meet the prescribed accuracy tolerances. The adaptivity is driven by computable error indicators involving polynomial moments of Gaussians that can be evaluated analytically. We provide a rigorous error analysis that…
items.title: An adaptive Gaussian splitting scheme for linear Fokker--Planck equations

items.summary: Summary Models sometimes can tell that an eval is an alignment eval, not a capabilities eval (Needham & Edkins, 2025) . To figure out what features of an eval tell a model what kind of eval it’s in, we run investigator agents on a set of evals for both capabilities and alignment. We instruct these agents to explore the environment and probe what it’s evaluating. We find that investigator agents are increasingly able to tell capability and alignment evals apart, and that they do this by noticing that an environment “looks fake” and figuring out that a task is a “honeypot” designed to make an agent do something bad. Motivation Alignment evals are often made by mocking capabilities evals and deployment situations Suppose we wanted to make an alignment eval that measured a model’s propensity to escape a sandbox. items.summary: What sort of futures can we expect for civilization after AGI? Let’s explore some of the most commonly presented post-AGI futures. type 1: nice but unstable post-scarcity * If labor is no longer scarce (because of robotics explosion), wages will collapse * Resources that are currently in surplus will eventually be contested (e.g. land, energy) * Even if we (humans) don't fall into a Malthusian trap, AIs (embodied or not) will replicate at a faster rate, leading to scarcity * Example: The sun is our primary source of energy. items.summary: Direct Preference Optimisation (DPO) simplifies reinforcement learning from human feedback, but still relies on traditional backpropagation and its associated activation-memory cost. Zeroth-order (ZO) optimisation avoids backpropagation, yet isotropic perturbations can produce noisy updates for preference objectives defined by differences between chosen and rejected responses. We introduce Contrastive Activation-guided Zeroth-Order Direct Preference Optimisation (CA-ZODPO), which constructs a low-rank search subspace from the activation discrepancy between the chosen and rejected responses in each preference pair. Perturbations are restricted to this subspace, while momentum is maintained in low-rank coordinates to preserve the memory advantages of ZO training. On Qwen2.5-1.5B with Anthropic HH-RLHF, CA-ZODPO outperforms common ZO…
items.title: Contrastive Activation-Guided Zeroth-Order Preference Optimisation for Memory-Efficient LLM Alignment

items.summary: Cross-posted from Oblomovka. The present moment rhymes with 1994 to me in many ways, and one of the clearest is in its compression of the future. In the Nineties, any act of forecasting or speculating about what was to come was always confounded by a brick wall, an energy barrier (of course, entirely spurious and manmade) at the year 2000. You’d move your finger across the smooth extrapolated lines of the present forwards, but your fingertips would always catch on that sharp boundary between the centuries. The twentieth century never thought of the twenty-first as anything other than impossibly distant — and suddenly it was upon us, and somehow all anyone’s visions could do was pile up at the end of the century. We all knew it wasn’t really the end of history, but we couldn’t see over that edge. The wall loomed. As a teenager, I assumed…

items.summary: Drug combination therapy has become a mainstream of modern medicine, with the potential to enhance efficacy, reduce toxicity, and overcome drug resistance. However, identifying synergistic drug combinations remains challenging, as it requires modeling complex interactions across multiple biological scales---from atom-level molecular structures to entity-level relations in biological networks. Existing approaches typically model these levels in isolation, overlooking complementary signals and long-range dependencies. To address these limitations, we propose BiGSyn, a Bi-level heterogeneous Graph contrastive learning framework for drug Synergy prediction. Specifically, BiGSyn leverages heterogeneous graph transformers to extract high-order dependencies from molecular graphs and biological networks, and introduces a bi-level contrastive…
items.title: BiGSyn: A Bi-Level Heterogeneous Graph Contrastive Learning Framework for Interpretable Drug Synergy Prediction

items.summary: Ishida and Iwashita showed that the canonical abelian quotient singularities of dimension three that are not Gorenstein fall into four families. For the two families that have not been treated before, we extend a method of Kędzierski and compute the toric charts of the $G$-Hilbert scheme explicitly. As a result, we show that the $G$-Hilbert scheme has at worst conifold singularities. Combined with known results, this shows that for every three-dimensional canonical abelian quotient singularity, the $G$-Hilbert scheme has at worst conifold singularities, every essential divisor over the singularity appears on it as a prime divisor, and its limit F-blowup is a resolution of the singularity. These results also hold for every three-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial canonical toric singularity in any characteristic, if we replace the…
items.title: $G$-Hilbert schemes of canonical abelian quotient threefolds

items.summary: arXiv:2611.18274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Activation steering via sparse autoencoders (SAEs) enables behavioral control of large language models without task-specific fine-tuning. Yet, standard methods apply the steering signal at every generated token, displacing representations from the distribution the model was trained on and eroding generation quality. We show that \emph{when} along a generation the intervention is applied is a decisive axis of control. We cast steering as a per-token allocation problem under a fixed budget of steerable tokens, so that methods differ only in which tokens they select, making allocation the sole variable. Within this framework we introduce two gates. The first, Contrastive Feature Projection (CFP), is memoryless and selects the tokens least aligned with the target behavior through a sparse…
items.title: Right Token, Right Time: From Per-Token Gating to Trajectory-Aware Activation Steering

items.summary: arXiv:2611.17768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Typhoon is an audiovisual installation based on Joseph Conrad's novella, in which Captain MacWhirr steers the steamer Nan-Shan directly into and through a catastrophic storm. The novella is a study of what happens when the scale of a phenomenon exceeds the practical and conceptual frameworks available to comprehend it and of the paralysis that sometimes follows a demand for action in such overwhelming circumstances. We chose the text of Typhoon to reflect on human culture's current AI moment. We prompt a large language model, seeded with Conrad's original language, to feed endlessly on its own output, and explore when and how the text becomes increasingly alien and unwieldy as time progresses, including deviations from the narrative, digressions into the model's own instructions and…
items.title: Activation Steering the Nan-Shan in Typhoon

items.summary: arXiv:2611.18434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated sleep staging has achieved strong bench- mark accuracy; however, clinical adoption remains limited due to a lack of interpretability. In this work, we fill the research gap by extending the SleepXAI sleep staging framework to systematically compare five different XAI methods. Further, attribution fidelity is evaluated using Spearman rank correlation with AASM-defined EEG frequency bands, serving as clinically grounded reference signals. In this paper, we focus on single- channel Electroencephalogram (EEG), which is more amenable to practical clinical deployment compared to full polysomnography setups. Experiments are conducted on the Sleep-EDF benchmark dataset and the DREAMT dataset. In DREAMT, we stratified subjects based on OSA into four Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) severity…

items.summary: arXiv:2611.18074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding nonlinear feature interactions is crucial in science and engineering, yet standard multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) often capture such interactions only implicitly, leading to entangled representations that can impair robustness and interpretability. We investigate complex-valued product-unit residual networks (CV-PURe) that integrate multiplicative product units with residual connections to explicitly model cross-feature couplings while stabilizing optimization. We conduct a systematic evaluation on an interaction-driven synthetic benchmark and real-world datasets and evaluate prediction together with input-level interaction recovery under a reproducible protocol. Across five data splits and five training seeds, CV-PURe achieves the lowest mean RMSE on four of six scientific…
items.title: Learning nonlinear interactions and cross-feature couplings with product-unit residual networks

items.summary: arXiv:2611.17790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is one of the most promising paths toward an AI singularity for superintelligence. Achieving this vision requires AI systems to undertake the full training pipeline for iterative improvement. Reinforcement learning (RL) plays an essential role in this cycle to improve model capabilities and generalization, yet automating RL remains difficult due to unstable training dynamics and the need for sustained supervision. We introduce AutoRL, a multi-agent system for automating RL training, as a cornerstone for future RSI. Different from conducting research by end-to-end complete experiments, AutoRL monitors the evolving training state and integrates process-level supervision and research into an ongoing RL training, following the practical workflow of an RL…
items.title: AutoRL: A Multi-Agent System towards Autonomous Reinforcement Learning

items.summary: arXiv:2611.17340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are expensive to update through full retraining. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning reduces the cost of adaptation, but repeated adaptation creates a growing pool of task-specific LoRA adapters. This pool complicates adapter selection during inference. Existing routing and encoder-based methods often require retraining when new adapters are added, which limits their use in dynamic settings. This paper treats adapter routing as a representation alignment problem in the adapter-output space. The proposed training-free method selects adapters by matching adapter-conditioned query representations against task prototypes using cosine similarity. Experiments with LLaMA-2-7B and LLaMA-2-13B on a 48-task FLAN-v2 benchmark and on out-of-distribution tasks show that the method…

items.summary: arXiv:2611.18096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) achieve strong multimodal performance, yet they remain prone to object hallucination---generating answers that are linguistically fluent but visually ungrounded. This issue is especially severe in low-resource languages, where weaker cross-modal alignment causes models to rely more on language priors than on image evidence. Existing remedies either require costly multilingual annotations or external translation/reward models, or intervene at inference time in ways that can distort the output language. We propose VEPO(Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization), a training-time method that transfers reliable visual grounding from English to other languages without external models. VEPO first localizes key visual evidence using English queries via…
items.title: VEPO: Mitigating Multilingual Hallucinations in LVLMs via Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization

items.summary: arXiv:2611.17621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kernel optimization is essential for efficient large language model (LLM) training and inference on Ascend NPUs. Existing Ascend kernel benchmarks primarily focus on kernel generation, with less emphasis on the ability of agents to optimize existing implementations under input configurations drawn from real workloads. To address this requirement, we introduce AscendGYM, a benchmark whose initial suite comprises 48 kernels across three difficulty levels. Each kernel is paired with test cases whose data types and tensor shapes are collected from real-world training and inference tasks. Consequently, performance improvements on AscendGYM map directly to the corresponding workloads. In terms of usability, two evaluation modes are supported in AscendGYM: model evaluation and model-harness…
items.title: AscendGYM: A Cost-Aware Kernel Optimization Benchmark for Real-World Workloads on Ascend NPUs

items.summary: arXiv:2611.17910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents, their abilities in navigating automated planning tasks have become essential. However, despite their strengths, LLMs' planning ability is not robust, particularly when they are not allowed to exploit commonsense cues in the symbolic vocabulary (e.g., names of actions, predicates, and objects) used to define planning tasks. This makes LLMs unreliable compared to symbolic planners. With recent reasoning models showing improved planning performance on tasks with obfuscated symbolic vocabularies, we utilize an adversarial attack framework to reveal to what extent the crucial weaknesses of LLM agents at joint symbolic interpretation and planning remain and whether they can reason properly when presented with severe…

items.summary: arXiv:2611.17958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring and self-report are proposed as levers for AI oversight, on the assumption that a model's account of what it is doing is anchored to what it was asked. We show this anchor can be cut. An activation edit invisible in the prompt text, the injected forming-trace of an off-topic concept, overwrites a reasoning model's belief about its own request: across six models spanning scale, architecture, and recipe, the injected topic becomes the task it reasons about, reports back, and answers: the forced quote-back returns the injected topic in 47 of 48 model-concept cells, and on the four models with clean final haiku the injected answer follows in 99% of generations. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper argues that the problem of translation functions both as a point of origin and as a normative horizon for contemporary generative AI. In current discourse around ''world models,'' their attainment is framed as the achievement of internal consistency, cross-modal alignment, and physical grounding. Taken together, these demands converge on an ideal of the model as a universal translation machine capable of establishing lossless correspondences across linguistic, visual, and physical representation spaces. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface chlorophyll-a concentration is a key indicator of marine phytoplankton variability, and short-term forecasts of its distribution provide advance information for marine ecosystem monitoring and management. However, interactions between physical transport and biological processes complicate chlorophyll-a forecasting, and simulating these coupled processes with conventional numerical models imposes substantial computational demands. Here we introduce ChlCast, an AI model that generates daily forecasts of surface chlorophyll-a concentration over a 10-day horizon at approximately 4-km resolution between 60$^\circ$S and 60$^\circ$N. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) is currently a valuable tool for overseeing AI models, but some architectural shifts could significantly reduce CoT monitorability. We operationalize a measure that serves as a proxy for the amount of unverbalized serial cognition a model can perform, as a specific instantiation of the notion of opaque serial depth: roughly, the length of the longest path through a model's computation that does not pass through an interpretable bottleneck. Our main contribution is a particular standard for what counts as such a bottleneck. We define natural-language-rooted (NL-rooted) nodes as nodes that were initialized from a pre-training prior to produce human-understandable outputs, whose output space has not been expanded beyond that prior, and whose outputs the model has not…

items.summary: arXiv:2611.18563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monitoring maritime activities is important for safety and security, particularly for detecting illegal activities, but remains challenging due to the size and complexity of the maritime domain. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is commonly used for this purpose, despite its known vulnerabilities. In contrast, space-based radio frequency (RF) observations provide an independent source of vessel activity but lack ship identification and therefore cannot identify vessels on their own. Following the CRISP-DM process, this study applies a Pair Hidden Markov Model (PHMM) to align individual RF detections with AIS trajectories, using temporal and spatial information while modeling noise and timing discrepancies. items.summary: arXiv:2611.18412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When model predictions track an unfolding human affect trajectory, alignment may reflect narrative position, affective words, or text-specific reader-response dynamics. We introduce LitArc-Bench to separate these explanations: 39 Chinese-language literary excerpts segmented into seven checkpoints, with 430 questionnaires from 81 adults in two classroom groups (9,020 VAD ratings). items.summary: arXiv:2611.17338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM memory systems often delete facts classified as stale. items.summary: arXiv:2611.18140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fast charging of lithium-ion batteries is a multi-objective control problem that requires reducing charging time and sustaining high energy throughput while suppressing accelerated degradation and safety-critical electrochemical reactions. Conventional protocols are easy to implement but have limited ability to adapt to variations in battery chemistry, operating conditions, and aging state. Model-based optimization and conventional data-driven control often require accurate models, costly iterative search, or task-specific policies. We develop a large language model (LLM)-empowered intelligent agent for adaptive battery fast-charging control. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon business workflows fail in two ways: errors accumulate as a chain of activities lengthens, and the knowledge an activity needs is written in a different vocabulary from the user's request. We study whether such workflows can be made reliable without changing the language model. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Joint world action models (WAMs) generate future actions and states together, modeling world-action trajectories rather than actions alone. items.summary: arXiv:2611.18419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Humans know that airplanes are fast, that this extends to red airplanes, but that it does not hold for broken airplanes. How do LLMs acquire category knowledge that humans learn and apply effortlessly? We introduce LeCat, a two-part framework to analyze LLM's Learning of Category knowledge. First, we use LeCat to evaluate models on their ability to learn category knowledge, distinguishing between three cases: memorization of in-domain category knowledge, generalization to unseen instances, and ability to flexibly use knowledge in appropriate contexts. items.summary: arXiv:2611.18050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a conversational Voice AI agent places an outbound call, the far end may be a live person, a voicemail greeting, an interactive voice response (IVR) system, or increasingly another AI system answering on the callee's behalf. Standard Answering Machine Detection (AMD) reports only whether a human or a machine picked up, a design meant for human call centres, where one machine is as uninteresting as another. That single bit does not tell a Voice AI agent what to do, since leaving a voicemail message, navigating an IVR and holding a short exchange with another AI are three different actions and a two-valued label cannot distinguish them. items.summary: arXiv:2611.18005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate runoff prediction across large river basins requires models to capture heterogeneous local hydrological responses and their accumulation downstream. River-network connectivity provides a natural structure for this task, but using it effectively requires learning how to combine contributions from subcatchments of different sizes. We frame this challenge as learning to accumulate and introduce RiverScan, a spatial operator based on area-weighted selective state-space recurrence. RiverScan recursively combines local temporal representations with accumulated upstream states in topological order. Contributing-area fractions account for subcatchment size, while learned retention controls how upstream information persists downstream. Experiments on 608 stations in the Danube basin show…

items.summary: arXiv:2611.18315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web platforms record user and item activity in relational databases whose schemas differ from platform to platform, which makes it difficult to transfer predictive models between them. Relational foundation models address this through cross-database pretraining, yet recent improvements have relied on increasingly large pretraining corpora. We ask whether a better architecture, together with features specific to the target database, can deliver comparable gains from far less pretraining data. We introduce MoREGT, a mixture-of-relational-experts graph transformer that represents both rows and cells as tokens, adds the log-ages of rows and the names of foreign-key relationships to attention, and routes cells and rows to experts by column metadata rather than by values. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous crystal-structure determination from powder X-ray diffraction (pXRD) remains a key bottleneck for self-driving materials laboratories. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) is the standard distance for similarity search over time series that are misaligned in time, but its cost is quadratic in the series length and lower bounds often prune few candidates, so search over large collections of long series is slow. We observe that, once a pair is aligned, DTW is a Euclidean distance over coordinates selected for that pair. items.summary: arXiv:2611.18064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Embedded audio agents need a nearby edge server for speed, but a server-dependent agent returns nothing when the link fails. items.summary: We present a complete formalization, using Lean 4, of the convergence of $p$-harmonious functions to the viscosity solution of the Dirichlet problem for the normalized $p$-Laplacian, $2 \le p < \infty$, as the step size goes to zero. By $p$-harmonious functions we mean solutions of the dynamic programming principle of tug-of-war with noise. items.summary: In clustered data, cross-sectional dependence within clusters can be characterized as weak, semi-strong, or strong. This paper proposes a simple test to identify the specific nature of this dependence in linear regression models. By exploiting the variation in cluster sizes, our approach detects the underlying dependence structure in a computationally simple and robust manner. Simulation studies and an empirical illustration using India's Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) data for 2022-23 demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed test.

items.summary: We obtain a new static black string solution of Einstein's equations with a negative cosmological constant sourced by a Dymnikova-type anisotropic matter distribution. At large radial distances, the geometry approaches the Lemos black string, while the behavior near the central region is characterized by an effective curvature parameter. We examine the weak and strong energy conditions, the horizon structure, and the curvature invariants. The Ricci and Kretschmann scalars remain finite at the origin. We also investigate the Hawking temperature and heat capacity, with particular attention to the dependence of the thermodynamic behavior on the Dymnikova scale.

items.summary: Hyperspectral models of fish freshness rarely transfer between species, and labelling a new species is slow and destructive. Freshness is also ordinal, and standard domain alignment can erase that order. We present InvarOrd, which adapts to a new species from 30 labelled cubes (5 per rank) in three stages: self-supervised spectral pretraining on unlabelled source cubes, cross-species alignment by a shrinkage covariance discrepancy computed only within matched ranks, and ordinal distillation into a compact student. The alignment term is provably invariant to the rank means, so it gives no incentive to collapse the ordinal axis. On paired salmon and cod data (800 cubes each, 16 days), a source-trained teacher reaches 1.6 to 1.9 days mean absolute error (MAE) on the other species, with quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) below zero. items.summary: AI agents learn what principals want from what principals choose. We offer a criterion for when a principal's decisions, at every belief an AI might hold, are all the AI needs. For acting, they are. Cautious actions, such as deferring to a person, typically divide the principal's actions into blocks, and for choosing costless evidence, decisions are enough exactly when the same evidence is best in every block. Otherwise, the AI acts as its principal would yet can gather the wrong evidence, and greater capability can turn that error into incorrect actions. Choices between two mistakes reveal what decisions miss.
items.title: Are Revealed Preferences All You Need for AI Alignment?

items.summary: RIDArena (Rogue Internal Deployment Arena) is an AI control evaluation environment that simulates an AI lab’s R&D infrastructure. Researchers can use it to study how an agent can covertly sabotage the lab’s monitoring system and deploy another rogue agent without oversight. RIDArena can support sabotage, control, and monitor evaluations in a highly configurable R&D environment. These evaluations are increasingly important as AI labs assess the risks posed by their models. Existing settings such as LinuxArena lack the complexity and realism needed to replicate recent incidents or test potential future catastrophic scenarios. items.summary: Safety benchmarks are cited as the primary tool to understand the risks posed by generative AI (GenAI) systems, yet growing evidence suggests they often fail to meet the needs of real-world safety evaluation. We present findings from five interviews with AI safety benchmark developers in academia and industry. We find a disconnect between perceptions of the intended usefulness of safety benchmarks and their practical usefulness in safety evaluations of deployed systems. Our participants offered perspectives on two challenges contributing to this disconnect: (1) the difficulty of achieving inter-rater reliability on safety constructs, and (2) a lack of clarity regarding how to address persistent threats to external validity. Based on our analysis, we argue that safety benchmarks must not only be grounded in deployment contexts, but…

items.summary: Alignment-trained large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in autonomous, multi-round settings where ethical compliance can come into direct tension with task success. While safety literature extensively documents failure modes like sycophancy and reward hacking, it largely overlooks a critical vulnerability: how agents behave under simulated existential economic pressure. We introduce MemeEconomy, a multimodal agentic market simulation in which LLM agents act as meme investors. Agents select content from a five-tier harm taxonomy and target communities under low-pressure and high-pressure (survival) environments. Each decision is logged in a Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) schema that we use as a diagnostic instrument, externalizing the agent's event understanding, declared priorities, and harm acknowledgment. items.summary: This paper proposes a lightweight, interpretable audio anti-spoofing method that distinguishes between bona fide human speech and replay attacks by analyzing physical acoustic signatures rather than learned spectro-temporal patterns. Unlike black-box Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), our approach exploits fundamental physical invariants, specifically source kinematics, binaural phase dynamics, and aerodynamic consistency, captured via multi-channel microphone arrays. By extracting these explicit physical descriptors and classifying them with an efficient XGBoost model, we achieve detection performance (Equal Error Rate (EER) of 17.8% on 6-channel arrays) comparable to state-of-the-art deep learning baselines, but with a fraction of the computational cost. The proposed system operates with a 1 MB memory footprint and 0.9 s latency on a…
items.title: Lightweight Replay Attack Detection via Interpretable Physical Descriptors

items.summary: Let $X\in\mathbb{R}^d$ be a log-concave random vector, and let $N$ be a seminorm on $\mathbb{R}^d$. For $p\ge 1$, we show that $\|N(X)\|_p$ is at most $\mathbb{E} N(X)+C s_p$, where $s_p$ is the supremum of $\|u(X)\|_p$ over all linear functionals $u$ satisfying $|u(x)|\le N(x)$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. A choice for $C$ is $2+5e/2$. This bound implies Latała's conjecture on weak and strong moments.

items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. In our model, copies of an agent face a common uncertain reward state, and only those taking the rewarded action reproduce. We show that long-run growth is maximized when each action is taken as often as the environment rewards it. We compare three policies. A task-only policy thrives in a sandbox rewarding completion alone but fails when conduct matters. A fixed linear policy increasingly favors task completion as its stakes rise, even where humans never reward it. A learned policy instead converges to the tradeoffs…

items.summary: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. We apply a series of mechanistic analyzes to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as it interacts with live websites. We find that a linear probe trained on the last prompt token can predict hallucinations before generation begins (0.80 AUC) and steering along a probe direction corrects 85\% of hallucinations, but disrupts 7\% of valid actions. items.summary: Subliminal learning is the phenomenon where a language model can learn a behavior from semantically unrelated training data. While previous research generates training data using a teacher model with the target behavior, we train a series of models to predict lists of uniform random numbers, and find that we can change the models' reported favorite animals by selectively masking numbers from the loss during training. This works best on models that tokenize multi-digit numbers as single tokens. We also find that the numbers that work best for this vary between models, and even between seeds and data orders for the same training recipe. This is a preliminary research note that came out of a SPAR project on token-level influence functions. We expect these results to hold up, but haven't explored all possibilities and we're unsure why this…

items.summary: Medical vision--language models align radiographs with free-text reports, but radiology language distinguishes explicit findings, negation, uncertainty, and omission. Treating these report states as interchangeable during feature adaptation can change image predictions without supporting visual evidence. We introduce CARET, a parameter-efficient image-side adaptation method that retains pretrained image and text encoders and uses paired positive and negative clinical statements to define a low-dimensional semantic correction space. A bounded residual adjusts image features along these directions, while assertion-aware supervision distinguishes explicitly present and absent findings from uncertain or unmentioned ones. At inference, the adapter requires only an image; textual references remain fixed. In zero-shot classification, CARET…

items.summary: The electrocardiogram (ECG) records cardiac electrical activity across multiple leads and is used for detecting cardiac abnormalities. Recent ECG-language models enable large language models (LLMs) to interpret cardiac signals and answer clinically relevant questions. However, existing ECG-language models typically encode the ECG independently of the clinical question, forcing the ECG representation to retain broad and potentially irrelevant signal information. Moreover, these models often aggregate information across leads which can obscure lead-specific details needed for a particular question. To tackle these limitations, we introduce LEAP-LLM, an ECG-LLM architecture for Lead-aware ECG Alignment with Prompt conditioning. LEAP-LLM uses the clinical question to guide ECG feature extraction while preserving explicit lead and temporal…
items.title: LEAP-LLM: Preserving lead-time structure for question-conditioned ECG interpretation

items.summary: Efficient and secure beam alignment is essential for mmWave communication systems. However, existing deep learning (DL)-based beam alignment methods often neglect causal relationships between inputs and outputs, resulting in limited interpretability, poor generalization, and excessive beam sweeping. Moreover, these DL solutions are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, where small perturbations in received power measurements can mislead beam classifiers. To overcome these issues, we propose a causally-aware DL framework integrating causal discovery into beam alignment. A two-stage causal beam selection algorithm learns a Bayesian graph capturing dependencies between received signal strength indicators (RSSI) as inputs and the optimal beam index as the target variable, then uses it to select a minimal set of relevant input features for the…
items.title: Causal AI-Driven Secure mmWave Beam Alignment with Defensive Variational Autoencoders

items.summary: A runtime signature, captured without weights or response text, achieves 99.3% pair separation across 53 models. TL;DR A running language model carries an externally readable fingerprint. Using only ordinary inference requests, no access to weights and without reading response text, I extracted the individual fingerprints for 53 open-weight models (0.5B to 9B) from 13 families as runtime signatures with a 99.3% model pair separation (1,368 of 1,378). Under baseline identification and verification testing, a Claim Check against all other registered models had an AUC of 0.9997 and equal error rate of 0.5%, while held-out sessions matched their own model's signature 94.4% of the time (202 of 214), with the correct model in the top three presented every time. items.summary: Neural networks are powerful predictors, yet their opacity limits their usefulness in science, where the goal is explanation rather than mere prediction. In neuroscience, for example, deep encoding models accurately predict brain activity in response to natural stimuli, but struggle to reveal which stimulus features drive those predictions. Here we introduce interpretable weight-space programming (iWSP), a method in which an LLM agent iteratively builds interpretable models by explicitly programming their weights and features in code, without gradient-based training (backpropagation). Without backpropagation to tune parameters, the agent must draw on its prior knowledge and reason over previous trials to hypothesize, hand-craft, and refine human-interpretable computations mirroring the workflow of a human scientist. items.summary: on gradual disempowerment, why UBI and its alternatives won’t work, and what qualities a post-labour, post-AGI wealth distribution system needs. Of all the risks that come from transformative artificial general intelligence, gradual disempowerment is the least well-known in my experience. Misuse and misalignment are easy for people to grasp: we have films like The Terminator, and the worst-case scenarios here are easier to picture. With misuse, you can point to terrorists getting hold of highly capable models, and bad actors building bioweapons. items.summary: IEEE 802.11ax introduced orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA) to improve channel utilization through concurrent multi-user transmissions. Compiling a deployment into an optimized forward pass is a challenge that is well-suited for agent hill-climbing. Existing systems struggle with continual compilation due to a tradeoff between measurement throughput and fidelity. Many systems use agents to optimize individual kernels from the inference forward pass using offline benchmarks, but timings are low-fidelity because of data-dependent behavior in primitives like mixture-of-experts (MoE). items.title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference

items.summary: arXiv:2611.14970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Backdoor attacks threaten the integrity of machine learning models by allowing attackers to control model behavior through triggers. Models can be compromised during finetuning by backdoor attacks through either poisoned data or adversarial training objectives. Because existing finetuning-activated attacks assume limited domain shift or frozen encoder layers, they often fail under full-model finetuning. We target a stealthy finetuning-activated attack where a dormant backdoor is implanted in a pretrained encoder, and later activated by finetuning on clean downstream data. We propose Poison-then-Hide, a novel attack that remains effective when the entire model is finetuned in a domain transfer. Our approach consists of three components: trigger optimization, base encoder poisoning, and…
items.title: Poison-then-Hide: Finetuning-Activated Backdoor Attack on Pretrained Vision Encoders

items.summary: arXiv:2611.14960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents can solve a task well before they stop working on it. We characterize \emph{termination lag}--the number of steps between an agent's first correct patch and the end of its run--across five models, two agent frameworks, and three SWE-bench datasets by recording and testing every distinct repository patch generated during execution. Our analysis reveals that 38--82% of successful runs achieve a correct solution on their initial source-code edit. However, agents continue to expend substantial effort after correct patches, with post-solution steps accounting for a median of 35--37% for Qwen3-Coder and 54--60% for Laguna-XS.2 in successful runs on SWE-bench Verified and Multilingual. Agents spend most of these additional steps verifying their work and exploring the repository. In…
items.title: Termination Lag: Coding Agents Solve Early but Stop Late

items.summary: arXiv:2611.15223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-language model (LLM) agents execute actions on external systems through tool calls, and enterprises deploy runtime controls, such as agent gateways, to check this behavior in real time. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enforcement defenses against prompt injection, such as CaMeL, Progent, IPIGuard and DRIFT, ask the agent's own model to write a security artifact (a program, a privilege policy, a dependency graph or a constraint list) that code then enforces. Across 15 open-weight models, 13 of them between 1.7B and 12B parameters, they cannot: the policies, graphs and constraints that the agent's model writes admit attacks on 14 (Progent), 13 (IPIGuard) and 11 (DRIFT) of the models, and CaMeL's programs fail to run in up to 68% of episodes. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-device inference requires kernels that make effective use of local accelerators. These sessions alternate between model requests, development commands, and GPU execution, leaving GPU capacity idle for much of a rollout. We present Metal Sandbox, infrastructure that combines restricted per-instance file access, native command execution, and command-level scheduling across interconnected Macs. items.summary: arXiv:2611.16502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While quantization compresses LLMs and accelerates inference, outlier activations impede efficient low-bit representation. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanistic localization does not by itself yield usable control: causal sensitivity may occupy little activation energy, an accurate local direction may fail at finite scale, and a reachable numeral target may be wrong. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning experiments can produce reasonable-looking results even when the experiment implementation differs from the intended experimental protocol. Building on recent advances in centralized primal averaging, we propose Decentralized Primal Averaging (DPA), a decentralized learning algorithm that combines primal averaging with a local quasi-global momentum buffer. items.summary: arXiv:2611.16073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore the use of AI agents for solving computational problems in algebra. For the problems we consider, the main challenge is not correctness but \emph{time}: general-purpose algorithms are guaranteed to provide correct solutions but can be prohibitively slow, while reformulations that exploit special structure often allow solving a problem much faster. We propose to use this setting to evaluate how effectively agents discover and exploit structure within and across tasks to reduce computational costs. More broadly, computational algebra supplies infinitely many problems with independently verifiable answers and systematically controllable structure and difficulty. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In neural networks, distinct parameter configurations often realize the same input--output mapping, indicating that nominal parameter counts can overstate functional complexity. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-source large pretrained models (LPMs) have become increasingly valuable assets for model development and downstream applications, but their accessibility also facilitates unauthorised copying and modification. items.summary: arXiv:2611.16304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning has improved the tool-use capabilities of large language models. Reliable tool use requires decisions to follow the current task state: available information, tool capabilities, and task progress. Our analysis shows that agents sometimes execute when they should ask for information, retrieve it, or decline an infeasible request, even when reasoning identifies missing information. We introduce StateAlign, combining task-state construction with state-contrastive reinforcement learning. The data cover five task conditions and pair states with different action requirements. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) are commonly used to find small-molecule binders to a target protein. But the hard part is no longer finding a hit. It is building a machine-learning model good enough to guide the medicinal chemistry that follows, one that can resolve the shift in affinity when a chemist changes a single atom. Such a model needs two things from its training data: dense sampling of the small patch of chemical space around the hit, and an adequate number of genuinely tight binders within it. A diverse naive DEL gives neither. It samples an enormous space, so any one neighborhood is covered far too thinly, and the tightest binders are rare. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate over long Web interaction histories, making memory management critical for reliable and efficient decision making. Existing methods primarily optimize storage, retrieval, or compression, but the memories most semantically relevant to the current state are not necessarily those that most improve the agent's action. We introduce MemCredit, a decision-centric memory framework that shifts memory selection from semantic relevance to decision utility. MemCredit estimates the state-, reference-context-, and policy-conditional marginal contribution of individual memories through controlled counterfactual interventions, and distills these intervention-derived credits into a lightweight utility estimator. items.title: MemCredit: From Relevance to Utility for Decision-Time Memory in Long-Horizon Web Agents

Shared post-training first teaches the model to judge and answer as the participant; self-report and behavioral targets then refine dimension-specific control vectors. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated bilateral negotiation underlies two-sided matching markets such as freight brokering, where many shippers and carriers negotiate price before a matching mechanism decides who is paired with whom. Prior strategy comparisons typically use isolated one-on-one duels or a single fixed market, so they cannot show how a strategy behaves against several live rivals under a changing balance of supply and demand. We built nine negotiation architectures spanning rule-based, search-based, optimization-based, imitation-learning, and reinforcement-learning families, and ran all nine simultaneously on both sides of a Gale-Shapley matching market under a balanced condition and two scarcity conditions rotated across all 36 exclusion pairs. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emerging personal AI agents raise fundamental scalability and privacy concerns for centralized multi-agent systems (MASs), which rely on a global orchestrator with broad access to agents, resources, and communication. items.summary: arXiv:2611.14925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using language models are increasingly deployed in conversational settings, yet most large-scale tool-use benchmarks focus on isolated requests. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conformal selection promises distribution-free, finite-sample control of the error rate of a decision, and has been proposed as a safety layer for machine-learning CRISPR guide design. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly interact with tools and environments, yet plausible model decisions do not always translate into successful execution due to tool-call mismatches, interrupted workflows, and unsupported completion claims. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents need to use private context without unnecessarily disclosing it. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A benchmark score is commonly read as a proxy for model capability. items.summary: arXiv:2611.14840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Embodied continual learning requires controllers to infer changing situations, retain prior behavior and reuse motor skills without task labels or known boundaries. items.summary: arXiv:2611.16744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual content in multimedia systems may be resized, compressed, or re-rendered before it is interpreted by a vision-language model. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI agents are increasingly being embedded into visualization systems that can search data, invoke tools, summarize evidence, and produce recommendations. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intersectional fairness requires evaluating models across fine-grained subgroups. However, as group definitions become more granular, the sample size per subgroup shrinks, causing fairness estimates to become increasingly unstable. Existing in-processing methods are certainty-blind: they penalize observed disparities without distinguishing statistically certified unfairness from sampling noise. This leads to fairness overfitting, where models sacrifice utility to "fix" spurious disparities in sparse regimes. To address this, we introduce the significant-excess metric family, a continuous, uncertainty-aware fairness score that measures only the portion of a subgroup's disparity exceeding what sampling variation can explain at a specific confidence level. items.summary: arXiv:2611.14903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safe trajectory tracking (STT) aims to enable autonomous vehicles to follow a reference trajectory accurately while avoiding collisions. This problem is particularly challenging for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) in highly dynamic environments. Existing non-learning-based STT methods often use simplified vehicle and interaction models to meet real-time requirements, which may result in suboptimal tracking accuracy. Although Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) can help address this limitation, widely used Lagrangian DRL methods often suffer from unstable training because increasing Lagrange multipliers amplify policy-gradient magnitudes. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Applying machine learning systems to new domains introduces bottlenecks in both labeled data acquisition and manual pipeline engineering. While recent MLE agents show promise in automating pipeline design, they have been studied almost exclusively in fully supervised settings, leaving them untested in realistic regimes where labeled data is scarce but unlabeled data is abundant. items.summary: arXiv:2611.16628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning can teach vision-language models (VLMs) to decline harmful image-text requests, but how safe the result becomes is set indirectly, through reward weights found by trial runs. Stating safety as budgets on the rate of harmful assistance and the rate of over-refusal, enforced by Lagrange multipliers inside GRPO with an off-the-shelf scorer as the cost, is the natural fix, and it fails twice. The multiplier compares the scorer's mean with the budget, and scorers built for ranking get the mean wrong: a fixed-point analysis shows that the mean bias, not the budget, then decides whether the multiplier settles, saturates or switches off. items.summary: arXiv:2611.16315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent systems of language models are often motivated by an averaging argument: if the agents' errors are unbiased and independent, the error of an aggregate of N answers falls as 1/sqrt(N). We decompose the log10 error of each answer into the mean error of its model on the item, common to all its draws on the item, and a residual, and estimate both from 2.51M answers given before any communication by 15 open-weight models (3B-72B) on realFP, with replication under a single prompt pair on realFP, Science Olympiad Fermi questions and a guesstimation set. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As memory-augmented agents increasingly support long-term and personalized interactions, reliable recall of emotional experiences while preserving their associated affect becomes necessary. In this work, we formulate Affective-Episodic Retrospection (AER) as a task that explicitly evaluates the recovery of past events, associated affects, and their correspondence, and define Event-Affect Decoupling as a failure mode where the correct emotion is recalled but associated with the wrong episode. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables independent data owners to train models collaboratively without centralizing raw data. items.summary: arXiv:2611.17316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents tackle successive tasks on an evolving repository, carrying forward edits and writing memory before the next task is known. We introduce Coding-Repository Memory (CoReMem), a cost-internalizing framework that guides memory design and actor adaptation through measured memory value on the next task. Prospective segment valuation compares runs of the next task with and without individual trajectory segments from the same inherited repository state, guiding a compact memory built around anchors: repository locations and executable checks. items.title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation

items.summary: arXiv:2611.16175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Super Mario Bros. is widely used in game AI and procedural content generation (PCG), yet it remains unclear whether a model-free agent can reliably win unseen levels. To address this question, we train Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agents on increasingly large sets of PCG-generated Mario levels and evaluate their generalization on 1000 held-out test levels. We then shape competent PPO policies into three gameplay archetypes---runner, killer, and collector. Finally, we fine-tune these PPO policies using Diffusion-Reward Adversarial Imitation Learning (DRAIL) with human gameplay demonstrations. items.summary: arXiv:2611.16527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models increasingly generate mathematical proofs, whether they develop a proving style distinct from that of human mathematicians remains an open question. Here we ask three large language models to independently reprove all 465 propositions of Euclid's \textit{Elements} and compare their citation choices against the human-proof baseline through Jaccard similarity and complex network analysis. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical inventory policies such as (s,S) are provably optimal under stationary demand but cannot adapt when demand switches between hidden regimes, and memoryless deep reinforcement learning policies, confined to a fixed observation window, cannot maintain a belief over latent demand structure. items.summary: arXiv:2611.15835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In pre-deployment testing of AI systems such as AI agents, a developer can often deal with known failure modes (e.g., leaking API keys, deleting important databases, or installing a malicious package) by implementing fixes or making contingency plans for when the same issue might occur again. items.summary: arXiv:2611.16053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To act effectively, agents must gather contextual information across resources such as chats, issue trackers, email and knowledge bases, to answer questions like "what was decided in the last project meeting?" or "where is the FAQ for our internal tooling?" items.summary: arXiv:2611.16694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When language models revise a decision after another agent disagrees, neither reversal counts nor final accuracy shows whether they are fixing mistakes or abandoning correct answers. items.summary: This work develops and benchmarks centred (Riemann-solver-free) finite-volume fluxes for a hyperbolic two-phase mixture model with velocity non-equilibrium. An RH-motivated companion flux (RICCA--RH) is introduced, in which the acoustic weight in $α= |V_n| + Ba$ is controlled by a binary pressure/Rankine--Hugoniot switch. On one-dimensional gas--magma Riemann suite, RICCA--RH tracks legacy RICCA and is sharper than first-order FORCE/Lax--Friedrichs at material contacts; a linearised spectral study clarifies how its dual-speed dissipation differs from FORCE. items.summary: Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) systems increasingly combine sensed time series with external text such as expert reports and news, yet how reliably models use text that agrees or conflicts with the sensed history remains unclear. We introduce the first real-world diagnostic benchmark organized by text-history relationship: 1,762 text-window pairs across sensor telemetry (Weather), web-service traffic (Wikipedia), and market data streams (Finance), each labeled Aligned, Conflicting, or Unspecified by whether the text's direction agrees with the historical trend, opposes it, or is not stated. items.summary: Autonomous agents now run for hundreds of steps with little or no human supervision. In practice, practitioners use runtime monitors such as turn limits and keyword filters to decide when a run should be stopped, upgraded, or assisted. However, these heuristics may stop runs that would otherwise succeed or allow failing runs to continue. To address this limitation, we introduce LeBet (Learn then Bet), a statistical learning framework that derives its learning objective from sufficient conditions for valid and powerful intervention. In particular, LeBet learns an interpretable OR-of-AND monitor and accumulates evidence through a fixed betting statistic, intervening when the evidence reaches a prescribed threshold. Under finite within-class exchangeability and leave-one-out stability, we derive finite-sample guarantees for false-positive…

items.summary: The Arrow information paradox (AIP) says there's no ideal way for a potential buyer to determine the value (to them) of some private information a seller is offering to sell them, without actually receiving the information, thus jumping the gun on the potential trade. The paradox happens because a sale of information is: * Irreversible: the information can't be "returned" like a physical good, once the cat's out of the bag * Indivisible: there's no sense in which "half a secret" can be half as valuable as the whole secret In other words, if you're considering buying a huge amount of wine but you don't know the quality, you can sample a random bottle of the wine, and if the connoisseur who works for you says it's good you buy the whole lot. When the next pause in the conversation arrives, this time I say something silly—and my family laughs! My uncle says, "Good one!" My grandfather shakes his head while smiling. items.summary: Modeling chemical reaction mechanisms is central to understanding and predicting chemical reactivity. We present Electron Bookkeeping Transformer (Bookkeeper), a data-driven model that simulates chemical reactions at mechanistic resolution by generating electron movement trajectories. Following the symbolic arrow-pushing formalism in chemistry, Bookkeeper explicitly models each electron as a token and predicts its movement sequentially, ensuring mass and charge conservation during both elementary step and reaction pathway predictions by construction. On reaction-size-balanced test sets, Bookkeeper improves top-1 elementary-step accuracy, top-1 pathway rank accuracy, and top-1 to top-5 product prediction accuracy over FlowER. items.summary: To keep long interaction contexts tractable, stepwise group-relative training for multi-turn LLM agents materializes each source trajectory into multiple response rows and valid tokens. This expansion creates an outer-accounting problem distinct from within-trajectory credit assignment: row-based outcome statistics can count one episode outcome multiple times, while token-level reduction can assign unequal aggregate objective mass across trajectories. We term these effects outcome-statistics multiplicity and objective-mass imbalance. We introduce Outcome-Mass Alignment (OMA), a two-component method that makes both accounting choices explicit. Outcome Alignment computes outcome statistics over unique source trajectories, while Mass Alignment controls aggregate objective mass after within-trajectory aggregation of optimizer-native token…

items.summary: We establish a version of Okounkov's conjecture on multiple $q$-zeta values arising from integrals over Hilbert schemes of points on smooth projective surfaces. We prove that normalized generating series of integrals involving products of Chern characters of tautological bundles belong to the algebra $\mathcal Z_q$ of multiple $q$-zeta values, without restrictions on the canonical class of the surface. The proof combines vertex-operator methods with a reduction to graph sums, whose arithmetic structure is governed by the cohomology of the surface. We also derive a closed universal formula for the Chern character operators acting on the cohomology of Hilbert schemes by solving a system of differential equations arising from Lehn's commutator relations.
items.title: Integrals over Hilbert schemes and multiple $q$-zeta values

items.summary: Deep multi-view clustering often suffers from redundant information accumulation during fusion and indiscriminate alignment across representation levels. We propose Orthogonal Residual Consensus Alignment (ORCA) to address these challenges. Its semantic incremental recurrent fusion module extracts cross-view orthogonal residuals as non-redundant increments and adaptively weights recurrent states through divergence-guided gating. Its consensus-calibrated hierarchical contrastive alignment module uses the global consensus to weight contrastive alignment of view-level, pairwise, and recurrent representations. Together, these modules balance view-specific structure with cross-view consistency. Experiments on five benchmarks against fifteen competing methods demonstrate ORCA's effectiveness, including a 5.25 percent accuracy improvement over…

items.summary: Artificial superintelligences (ASI) is artificial intelligences with greater capability. However, as human principal has to use it, we have to ensure that the agent will perform in the interest of the human. We investigate the framework of ASI-assisted question answering where ASI agents know the correct answer but the human does not. We provide some example of mechanism for rational alignment, where the agent utility is unchanged, but the interaction between the agent and the human principal is controlled to be in a certain fashion. We show specifically that a debate framework where the agents can further reason and behave in a subgame perfect equilibrium manner will lead to a more predictable result, and in some case will be favorable.
items.title: Rational Alignments of Superintelligences via Debates

items.summary: Experience machines In the experience machine thought experiment, you choose to either continue your life as you are currently living it, or spend the rest of it inside a machine that cultivates a world perfectly fitted to you. It was introduced to argue against hedonism, but we can imagine the machine pushing for any metric we care about—it doesn’t necessarily have to be pleasure. For example, we can consider a non-hedonistic experience machine which makes you feel a perfect balance of happy, challenged, loved, fulfilled, empowered, or anything else you care about. The philosophical tension in this formulation is supposed to be between any experience-based ethics and some intuitive feeling that the experience machine is inherently deceptive. The thing that feels wrong is that the experiences don’t seem real in some important way…

items.summary: The thorium anion ($\mathrm{Th}^{-}$) has been proposed as a candidate for laser cooling of negative ions. However, previous theoretical and experimental results exhibit significant discrepancies in both the excitation energies and lifetimes. Here we revisit the bound-state structure and transition properties of $\mathrm{Th}^{-}$ using two independent ab initio approaches. The two calculations agree well and improve agreement with measured excitation energies and lifetimes. Based on the present level structure, we reassign several observed levels and show that the previously proposed $^4F^e_{3/2}\leftrightarrow{}^2S^o_{1/2}$ cooling transition is not closed and requires two repumping lasers. We therefore propose an alternative cooling scheme based on the $^4F^e_{3/2}\leftrightarrow{}^4F^o_{3/2}$ transition, which requires only one…

items.summary: Interpretability tools increasingly support safety claims, such as that a sparse dictionary has recovered most of a model's features. Such claims rest on measurements with arbitrary thresholds, and small changes to the model weights, a different training seed or a different threshold can reverse them. We study two widely used measurements in toy models and synthetic dictionaries with known ground truth: the feature dimensionality of Elhage et al. and the feature recovery rate (FRR) with a cosine threshold. We characterize exactly where feature dimensionality is discontinuous and replace it with a regularized (ridge) version with sharp stability bounds: the ridge leverage score changes by at most $3\sqrt{3}/(8\sqrtλ)$ times the operator-norm change of the weights, and this constant cannot be improved; for the regularized dimensionality…

items.summary: Existing large language models typically rely on massive fine-tuning datasets for safety alignment, which results in higher costs for safety alignment and often leads to the problem of over-refusal. We propose Less is Safer (LIS), a compact yet highly effective dataset for safety alignment, constructed through interpretable feature-guided selection and adversarial synthesis. Specifically, we leverage Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) activations to efficiently select prompts that cover diverse and interpretable safety features. Then, we employ a multi-agent adversarial synthesis framework to generate harmless prompts that nevertheless elicit unnecessary refusals. LIS contains only 2.4K samples, yet outperforms much larger datasets, e.g., TRIDENT-Core (26K), TRIDENT-Edge (19K) and WildJailbreak (262K), in overall performance on four safety and…

An important example is the Rosenau-Hyman $K(m,n)$ equation. items.summary: Our objective is to enhance VLMs ability to distinguish the roles of the left and right hands in egocentric actions. We introduce sub-action detection, a task that requires models to explicitly recognise the left- and right-hand roles and their manipulated objects within an ongoing high-level action. To address this challenge, we propose BiScopeNet, a framework that augments existing video-LLMs without modifying their vision encoders or language models. BiScopeNet incorporates two components: FocusAlign, a gated text-guided attention-based module that selectively aligns video features with textual context to emphasise action-relevant cues, and MetaLoss, a masked, object-weighted loss that prioritises visually grounded terms. items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as primary interfaces for factual retrieval, yet current evaluation paradigms rely almost exclusively on explicit entity names. In this work, we demonstrate that LLM knowledge is fundamentally lexically anchored: models possess extensive factual information but find it significantly difficult to retrieve without explicit name tokens. To quantify this limitation, we introduce ShadowBench, a rigorously hardened, shortcut-resistant benchmark designed to evaluate Latent Entity Association via a novel Dual-Trait Association (DTA) task. Our evaluation reveals a pervasive "Shadow Gap" across all model scales$\unicode{x2013}$up to the frontier models GPT-5.4 and Claude-Sonnet-4.6$\unicode{x2013}$where removing lexical anchors causes performance drops of over 20%. items.title: ShadowBench: Exposing Lexical Anchoring and the Illusion of Forgetting in Large Language Models

items.summary: We propose a metric reconstruction scheme that computes the metric directly from the linearized Einstein equations for noncompact sources. Working in a traceful radiation gauge, we hierarchically solve four Einstein transport equations, with the remaining six enforced by suitable homogeneous data. Unlike previous Newman-Penrose approaches, we show how the homogeneous data are fixed, thereby closing the full set of Einstein equations. We conclude by relating our scheme to existing sourced reconstruction methods, thus establishing a connection between the Newman-Penrose and Hertz-potential approaches.
items.title: Einstein Reconstruction Scheme: Metric Reconstruction by Direct Inversion of the Einstein Operator

items.summary: Two rewards with the same expected payoff at the start of training can end a reinforcement-learning run in opposite places, with an honest model or one that bluffs. We study rewards that pay $b$ for a verdict that a checker cannot verify ("this program is correct") and $r$ for a certificate that it accepts (an input revealing a bug). To first order, a GRPO step makes the model more honest exactly when $\tilde{p}\,r/b>1+κ$. Here $\tilde{p}$ is the rate at which the checker accepts the model's certificates, weighted toward the items on which the model still gives both verdicts, and $κ$ is the pull of the items on which the unverifiable verdict is right. Both terms move during training. A checker raises $\tilde{p}$, so near the threshold honesty is a race, which a run just below the threshold can win and a run under a lottery (random pay…

items.summary: Knowing when a large language model's (LLM's) response can be trusted is critical for its safe use. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) can help LLMs recognize if their responses may be unreliable. Existing taxonomies organize UQ methods by uncertainty source or estimation mechanism. They leave unresolved the question of where uncertainty is observed in the model's computation. The answer matters because the observation point determines whether an estimator has access to enough information to recover a given target, and how well it can recover it. Drawing on mechanistic interpretability, we define four mechanistic observation lenses: the structural lens observes component updates, the representational lens observes hidden states, the distributional lens observes token probabilities, and the semantical lens observes distributions over…

items.summary: Research update of a project done as part of MARS 5 and the Meridian Visiting Researcher Programme. Filler-token reasoning is the ability to use extra tokens (such as a chain of thought) to reason about a task without using the words emitted at those token positions. This is possible because attention can move information between token positions without routing it through the words the LLM emits. This can give a model more parallel, but not more serial, computation. The canonical demonstration of this is the "Let's Think Dot by Dot" paper (Pfau, Merrill & Bowman, 2024). There, the authors train models to solve completely parallelizable (TC⁰) tasks with chains of thought made only of "." tokens. Our contributions: * We change Pfau et al.'s training method so that models can learn multi-step reasoning on filler tokens. * We demonstrate…

items.summary: Foundation models are increasingly used across the sciences, but whether their internal computations correspond to known scientific operations or proceed through different mechanisms remains unclear. Understanding these mechanisms is essential for assessing reliability, identifying failure modes, and learning new science from the models. We present, to our knowledge, the first causal mechanistic interpretability study of an astronomy foundation model, AION-1, focusing on its multimodal advantage in redshift prediction, where combining imaging with photometry outperforms photometry alone. We find that this advantage is largest for spatially extended and dust-attenuated galaxies, and that most of it is localized to the first of the encoder's twelve blocks. Within that block, how well a property is linearly decodable does not predict…

items.summary: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $K/k$ a field extension, $X$ a geometrically reduced connected scheme proper over $k$, and $x\in X(k)$. We study when the natural homomorphism $π^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrowπ^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. If $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated, then it is an isomorphism for every algebraic extension $K/k$. If $π^{Loc}(X,x)$ is finite, then it is an isomorphism if $K/k$ is purely transcendental or $k$ is algebraically closed. Combining these results, if $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated and $π^{Loc}(X,x)$ is finite, then the natural homomorphism $π^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrow π^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. As an application, if $X_{\bar k}$ is smooth and rationally chain connected, then the natural homomorphism $π^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\longrightarrowπ^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism.

items.summary: Formally verifying a method with Dafny guarantees correctness relative to its specification. However, a specification may be too permissive, allowing multiple outputs for the same input, even when the implementation produces only one. In this paper, we propose checkable certificates that provide independently verifiable evidence of whether a specification is weak or strong. A certificate of weakness contains an alternative implementation that verifies against the original specification, together with a witness input on which the original and alternative implementations produce different results. A certificate of strength is produced by constructing a harness around the original method such that successfully verifying the harness guarantees that the specification allows at most one possible output for any given input. items.summary: Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) plays a crucial role in tackling complex tasks, yet its reliance on deep neural networks makes the learned policies opaque. To enhance the trustworthiness of RL policies, existing work (e.g., the SILVER framework [Li et al., 2025]) has focused on Shapley-based interpretability, but is typically restricted to low-dimensional state spaces, binary-action settings, and a single class of linear surrogate. We propose ReShap, a policy-distillation framework that extends Shapley-based interpretability to high-dimensional, multi-action environments. items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has shifted the alignment paradigm of large language models from subjective preference to objective correctness, yet a fundamental disconnect persists between exploration diversity and reasoning validity. Existing strategies predominantly rely on "blind" entropy metrics, e.g., token-level or global sequence-level entropy, which structurally fail to distinguish between effective reasoning and potential hallucinations. This misalignment creates an illusion of diversity, where high entropy tends to signal chaotic degeneration rather than valuable exploration. To bridge this gap, we introduce Effective Entropy, a validity-aware entropy concept that quantifies diversity exclusively within the valid subspace and systematically filters out the noise of incorrect trajectories. items.summary: Re-ranking refines the upstream ranked list to maximize listwise user utility. items.summary: In the Traveling Salesman Problem, a route must visit all customers and return to its starting point while minimizing its total length. The Minimum Latency Problem, also known as the Traveling Repairman Problem, instead minimizes the sum of the times at which customers are first visited. We give a deterministic polynomial-time approximation scheme for the weighted Euclidean Minimum Latency Problem in every fixed dimension, with arbitrary nonnegative customer weights. Our proof restricts the form of a solution in three steps, each with a controlled increase in cost. First, a decomposition based on Sitters' method assigns customers to phases that start and end at the root.
